newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Diana heads for Angola to visit landmine victims.
newsitem.headline: Diana heads for Angola to visit landmine victims.

text.p: Britain's Princess Diana arrives in Angola on Monday to visit landmine victims in a trip expected to boost her status as a goodwill ambassador for Britain.
The glamorous princess, who once said she wanted to be the "queen of people's hearts", will back the Red Cross campaign against anti-personnel mines.
Angola typifies the dangers of landmines -- the country has the world's record number of amputees thanks to mines sown during two decades of civil war.
About 70,000 Angolans have lost limbs in blasts from mines used in the war that broke out on independence from Portugal in 1975.
Along with Cambodia and Afghanistan, Angola is the most mined country in the world and aid agencies consider this the single biggest factor hindering economic and reconstruction in rural areas.
At least five groups are helping to clear the millions of mines that remain from the war between the government and rebel UNITA movement, in which hundreds of thousands of people were killed.

The princess will the guest of the British Red Cross, which is campaigning with the International Committee of the Red Cross and International Federation of the Red Cross for a worldwide ban on landmines.
Diana, whose marriage to British royal heir Charles ended last August, will probably also visit a minefield during her visit that will be followed by about 200 journalists, organisers said.
Angolans said they hoped the visit would help focus attention on the country's efforts to implement a 1994 peace plan.
"We heard this on the radio. It is good that she is coming to see the suffering of the Angolan people," vendor Fernando Sebastiao said.
Diana will stay at the high-security residence of British Ambassador Roger Hart, set among the residences of government officials on a hill looking out on the Atlantic Ocean.

"She is coming here as a British Red Cross volunteer to gain understanding of the mine problem in Angola and talk to a number of victims and see for herself the situation," Michael Stone of the British Red Cross told reporters.
President Jose Eduardo dos Santos will host her at a dinner at his presidential palace outside the city on Monday night.
On Tuesday she will visit local Red Cross health posts and landmine training centres as well as an orthopaedic centre.
The following day Diana will travel by air to the central highlands capital of Huambo where she will see a demonstration of landmine lifting operations by the British-based Halo Trust group.
